outline: This course deals with management accounting and control both within a micro-behavioural and within an organisational theory perspective. The aim is to provide an understanding of the developments in management accounting and control theory and practice and the implications of critical variables that affect the design, development and operation of management accounting and control systems. Practical aspects of management accounting are mainly examined through computer assisted learning (CAL). Students are expected to cover the prescribed reading on their own, and to perceive the taught seminars as the opportunity to ask questions and to offer their views at any time.
schedule:
1. Introduction
2. Financial Statement Introduction
3. Introduction to Managerial Accounting and Job Order Cost systems
4. Cost Information for Decisions
5. Job Costing System
6. Variable Costing System
7. Process Cost Systems
8. Target Costing and Price Planning
9. Profit Reporting for Management Analysis
10. Midterm exam
11. Standard cost system
12. Balanced Scorecard & Strategy Maps
13. Performance Evaluation Using Variances
14. Statement of Cash Flows
15. Lecture
16. Financial Statement Analysis
17. Capital Investment Analysis
18. Final exam
assessment:
Assignment Quits&Participant 40%
Midterm exam 30%
Final exam 30%
